subject: Commercial: conversion crediting & seat-token offset structure (FastFinance RFP)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@fastfinance.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@fastfinance.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial appendix and proposed conversion-crediting approach

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks again for the RFP runbook — attached is the commercial appendix that maps our token pricing to the use-case profiles you included. The key piece we wanted to call out is the conversion-crediting mechanism you requested: instead of a pure seat-based uplift we propose a hybrid "seat-token offset" that credits tokens back to the commercial bucket whenever paid seats convert to active API usage.

High-level:
- Base commit: 5M tokens/month (anchored rate)
- Seat add-ons: per-seat monthly fee covers 200k tokens of predictable usage per seat; excess usage consumes committed tokens first and then billed overage at the variable rate.
- Conversion credit: if a paid seat (user license) triggers >5000 API calls per month, we apply a token credit equal to 40% of the incremental tokens consumed by that user for up to 6 months (pilot window). Credits reduce overage drawdown, not the committed baseline.

Why this structure? It aligns incentives: FastFinance only pays unit costs for seats that materially drive inference usage, and Redwood reduces apparent overage volatility during onboarding. The attached spreadsheet contains the worked examples with blended effective rates.

Attachments: 20261020_FastFinance_Commercial_Appendix.pdf, conversion-credit-model.xlsx

Next steps: happy to walk through numbers with your procurement team. If this structure looks acceptable we can bake the credit rules into the MSA addendum and include a simple clause for annual reset/true-up.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the appendix. A couple of clarifying Qs from procurement and our platform team: 
1) How do credits behave if a seat churns mid-month? Do we get a pro-rated credit or is it forfeited?
2) Is the 40% conversion-credit a hard cap per user or capped by overall monthly seat quota?
3) Can credits be carried forward against future months' overages, or do they expire at the end of the 6-month pilot window?

Also, procurement asked for an illustration where we assume 12k monthly active seats with a 10% activation-to-API rate — can you show the blended per-token effective price under that scenario?

If possible, can you loop in the person who owns billing ops so we can align on invoice treatment?

Best,

Proposed internal split of work:

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Commercial appendix and proposed conversion-crediting approach -- procurement follow-ups

Jonas / team — attached is an updated workbook (conversion-credit-model.xlsx) with the 12k-seat illustrative tab and a churn pro-rate tab. Summary answers for the customer:

1) Churn handling: we recommend pro-rata credits for seats that churn mid-month (credit = monthly-credit-amount * days-active/30). For rapid churn scenarios we provide a monthly reconciliation cadence to avoid gaming.
2) Cap mechanics: the 40% credit is per-user on incremental usage above the 5k free threshold; however we also apply a monthly global cap equal to 25% of total monthly committed tokens to limit exposure for the vendor. This hybrid cap protects Redwood while keeping the mechanics simple for FastFinance.
3) Expiry/rollover: credits can offset overages for up to 6 months; any unused credits after month 6 expire. We do not allow credits to increase committed baseline — credits are strictly for overage offset.

Billing ops (Ben) — I added a sample invoice stub in the workbook showing a separate line item: "Conversion Credits (offset)". That makes reporting transparent and leaves committed-line items untouched.

I'll tidy the workbook and hand the contract paragraph to Lauren.

Attachments: conversion-credit-model.xlsx

Marissa Cole
Senior Commercial Analyst | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial appendix and proposed conversion-crediting approach — updated examples and draft clause

Alicia / Tom — attaching the updated commercial appendix and an illustrated workbook with the 12k-seat example (see tab "12k-seat scenario"). Key points inline:

- Churn: we recommend pro-rata credits; example shows a 12% churn scenario with month-by-month credit reconciliation.
- Credit caps: 40% per converting user with a monthly global cap set to 25% of committed tokens (protects against mass activation shocks).
- Expiry: credits usable for up to 6 months, expire thereafter; cannot be used to inflate committed baseline.
- Invoice treatment: credits appear as a distinct invoice line item that reduces billed overage for the period. Year-end true-up will reconcile remaining credits vs. committed consumption.

Attached: 20261020_FastFinance_Commercial_Appendix.pdf, conversion-credit-model.xlsx
Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/FF-2026-1467 (hubspot record)
DocuSign LOI (if you want to lock in the pilot): https://docusign.com/FF-2026-1467-pricing-LOI

If that aligns I can ask Legal to include the short paragraph below in the MSA addendum: 

"Conversion credits: During the pilot window (six months from the effective start date), Redwood will apply conversion credits to FastFinance's billed overages. Credits are calculated per qualifying converted seat at the agreed rate and will be pro-rated for partial-month seat churn. Total credits applied in any month shall not exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of Customer's committed token volume for that month. Unused credits expire at the end of the six-month pilot and shall not be applied to increase committed volumes. Credits will be reflected as a separate line item on monthly invoices and reconciled at annual true-up."

Next step: please confirm acceptance of the pilot mechanics and whether procurement wants the pilot start to be tied to the first paid invoice or a predefined calendar date.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
